doc_verification.detail: Reachability: no doc_preflight sidecar exists for this batch, so verified directly — curl GET https://api.qdrant.tech/v-1-18-x/api-reference/aliases/get-collection-aliases returned HTTP 200 (Fern-hosted page; WebFetch tool itself could not pass domain verification, direct HTTP fetch succeeded). Version: URL carries v-1-18-x slug and the page HTML version selector shows 'v1.18.x' (PASS). Content: page title 'List collection aliases', description 'Retrieves a list of all aliases for the specified collection', response section documents ONLY a 200 'successful operation' with result.aliases[].{alias_name, collection_name} — the assertion's first clause (200 + list of {alias, collection_name}) IS in the doc; the second clause '404 for an unknown collection' is NOT present anywhere in the v-1-18-x page (nor in the unversioned latest api-reference page, both checked via .md variant and full HTML keyword scan) (PARTIAL). Endpoint precision: contract endpoint_registry contains 'aliases+collection+list' GET with source_url matching, and the route exists in source (src/actix/api/collections_api.rs:94 #[get("/collections/{collection_name}/aliases")]) (PASS). No SDK/REST confusion: the gRPC/SDK faces call the same server handler.

secondary_observations: log(same script, earlier probe): probe [nul-byte] name='a%00b' -> status=422; raw: {"status":{"error":"Validation error in path parameters: [collection_name: collection name cannot contain \"\u0000\" char]"},"time":0.0} — NUL name rejected by REST path validation

rest face (live re-probe 2026-09-02, same endpoint): GET /collections/__no_such_collection_zzz__/aliases (plain unknown name, no malformed chars) -> http=200, code=0 {"result":{"aliases":[]},"status":"ok","time":0.000010308} — identical disposition to the lone-surrogate probe; the 200 is NOT caused by the malformed character
rest face (live re-probe): GET /collections/x%ED%A0%80y/aliases (primary reproduced) -> http=200 {"result":{"aliases":[]},"status":"ok"} (time 0.000017-0.000029)
rest face (live): GET /collections/a%2Fb/aliases (encoded-slash) -> http=422 'collection name cannot contain "/" char' — percent-decoding happens BEFORE validation, and '/' is rejected
rest face (live): GET /collections/c%01d/aliases (control char 0x01) -> http=200 {"result":{"aliases":[]},"status":"ok"} — control chars other than NUL pass the legacy path validator

rest face same-family existence-checking endpoint (live): GET /collections/x%ED%A0%80y -> http=404, body 'Not found: Collection `x\ufffd\ufffd\ufffdy` doesn't exist!' (echo bytes \xef\xbf\xbd x3) — the server lossily decoded %ED%A0%80 into three U+FFFD replacement chars, i.e. a legal UTF-8 name; the application logic never saw an illegal/lone-surrogate string, and existence-checking endpoints 404 this name exactly like any plain unknown name
rest face same-family exists endpoint (live): GET /collections/x%ED%A0%80y/exists -> http=200 {"exists":false} — identical to plain-unknown baseline {"exists":false}

cross-script (state_001 log): [NEG-1:never-created] status=200 {"result":{"aliases":[]},"status":"ok"} while its [control:describe never-created] status=404 'Not found: Collection `salc_del_never_created_1788354857` doesn't exist!' — collection-info endpoint 404s unknown collections, the aliases-list endpoint does not

http_semantics.note: A collection name that (per contract clause 2) should 404 — whether malformed-bytes (lone-surrogate) or plainly unknown — returns HTTP 200 with a full success envelope (status:'ok', result.aliases:[]) and no error code at all; the 404 diagnostic branch does not exist server-side, so the client error (if the 404 semantics is the correct one) is masked as 2xx success

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: returns 200 with a list of {alias, collection_name}; 404 for an unknown collection
contract_grounding.note: The observed 200+ok for the lone-surrogate name (which the server lossily decodes to the legal name 'x\ufffd\ufffd\ufffdy') falls genuinely inside the quoted constraint's second domain (unknown collection name — plain-unknown names show the identical disposition), so violates=true for the 404 clause; however the 404 clause itself is doc-unsupported (v-1-18-x api-reference documents only 200) and source-unsupported (v1.18.0 handler performs no existence check), so the contradiction is contract-vs-(doc+implementation), not a malformed-name acceptance inside the application.

chain_links: doc:api.qdrant.tech v-1-18-x 'List collection aliases' page (HTTP 200; only a 200 response documented; no 404/unknown-collection prose)
chain_trace.break_detail: All four links are present and the wire observation (200+ok empty aliases) is verified by live re-probe, but the contract's second clause '404 for an unknown collection' is not grounded in the cited documentation page (v-1-18-x documents only 200 'successful operation') and the endpoint_registry doc_quote with the same 404 phrase is an annotator summary not traceable to the page; the implementation likewise contains no 404 branch for this endpoint, so doc and code agree with each other and the 404 clause is the anomalous link.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST route GET /collections/{collection_name}/aliases (collections_api.rs:94) -> Path<CollectionPath> validator (mod.rs:46-53; legacy rule bans only '/' and NUL, length 1..=255) -> do_list_collection_aliases (common/collections.rs:167) -> toc.collection_aliases (toc/mod.rs:434) -> alias_persistence.collection_aliases (alias_mapping.rs:114) which scans the alias map and returns [] when the name matches no collection; nowhere in the chain is collection existence checked and no StorageError::NotFound can be raised, so 200+empty-aliases for unknown collections is the structural behavior of v1.18.0. The gRPC face (tonic collections_api.rs:145) shares do_list_collection_aliases, so the same 200-empty semantics apply there. Empirical decode check: server error echo shows %ED%A0%80 is decoded lossily to three U+FFFD chars ('x\ufffd\ufffd\ufffdy') before validation, and U+FFFD is not in INVALID_CHARS, so the effective name is legal and creatable; char validation fires only for NUL and '/' (observed 422s) and cannot fire for this value.
source_grounding.note: The validation the constraint's second clause requires (a 404 diagnostic for an unknown collection, which the claim's 'expected 4xx' relies on) does not exist in the v1.18.0 source: the handler chain contains no existence check and no NotFound branch for any collection name. The claim's specific premise ('the lone-surrogate name cannot legally exist, so accepting it is illegal') does not hold at application level because the server lossily normalizes the bytes to the legal name 'x\ufffd\ufffd\ufffdy' before any validation or lookup. by_design_in_source not recorded: no code comment/docstring in this path declares an intentional no-404 behavior (no explicit intent evidence found).

mundane_explanation.surviving: What survives: v1.18.0 GET /collections/{collection_name}/aliases has no unknown-collection existence check — every unknown name (plain, control-char, or lossily-normalized lone-surrogate) returns 200 + empty aliases while the contract asserts 404 for unknown collections; the vendor's own v-1-18-x API reference documents only 200, and the aliases code path contains no 404 branch — so the observed wire behavior is exactly what the source implements and what the doc describes, and the asserted 404 semantics is the unsupported element. The claim's Type1_IllegalSuccess reading ('malformed name accepted') additionally rests on a premise the evidence refutes: the malformed bytes never reach application logic as an illegal name (lossy decode to legal U+FFFD chars) and the identical 200 occurs for legal plain unknown names (boundary_004).
